questions.enonce_markdown:
Briefly explain the following as used in database.

(a) Flat file. (1 mark)

(b) DBMS. (2 marks)

(c) Transitive dependency. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Flat file (1 mark).** A flat file is a simple database made of one single table (a text file, a CSV file or a spreadsheet) in which all the data are stored in rows and columns, with no relationship with other tables; the same data are often repeated many times.

**(b) DBMS (2 marks).** A Database Management System is the software used to create, store, organise, retrieve, update and protect the data of a database (for example MySQL, Microsoft Access, Oracle). It lets users and programs use the data without knowing how it is stored, controls who may access it, keeps the data consistent and provides backup and recovery.

**(c) Transitive dependency (2 marks).** A transitive dependency exists when a non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute and not directly on the primary key: if A determines B and B determines C (with B not a key), then C depends on A only indirectly. Example: in a table STUDENT(StudentID, ClassCode, ClassName), ClassCode depends on StudentID and ClassName depends on ClassCode, so ClassName depends transitively on StudentID. Such dependencies must be removed to reach Third Normal Form (3NF), by putting ClassCode and ClassName in a separate table.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Convert $1111011_2$ to octal and to hexadecimal. (3 marks)

(b) Explain why the binary number system is used in computing than decimal. (2 marks)

(c) State the hierarchy of units of time from picoseconds to milliseconds. Hence convert $2 \times 10^{-6}$ ms to nanoseconds. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Conversion (3 marks).**

*To octal:* group the bits in threes from the right: $1\ 111\ 011$, that is $001\ 111\ 011$, which gives $1\ 7\ 3$. So $1111011_2 = 173_8$.

*To hexadecimal:* group the bits in fours from the right: $111\ 1011$, that is $0111\ 1011$, which gives $7\ B$. So $1111011_2 = 7B_{16}$.

*Check:* $1111011_2 = 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 2 + 1 = 123$; $173_8 = 1 \times 64 + 7 \times 8 + 3 = 123$; $7B_{16} = 7 \times 16 + 11 = 123$.

**(b) Why binary is used (2 marks).** A computer is built from electronic circuits (transistors and switches) that have only two stable states: on and off (high and low voltage). These two states represent the two binary digits 1 and 0 directly. Binary circuits are simple, cheap and very reliable, since it is easy to tell two voltage levels apart even with some electrical noise, whereas ten levels would be needed for decimal; and all data (numbers, text, sound, images) and instructions can be encoded in bits and handled with Boolean logic.

**(c) Units of time (3 marks).** From the smallest to the largest, each unit being 1000 times the previous one:

picosecond (ps, $10^{-12}$ s) < nanosecond (ns, $10^{-9}$ s) < microsecond ($\mu$s, $10^{-6}$ s) < millisecond (ms, $10^{-3}$ s).

Conversion: $1\ \text{ms} = 10^{-3}\ \text{s} = 10^{6}\ \text{ns}$ (because $10^{-3} / 10^{-9} = 10^{6}$). Therefore

$$2 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{ms} = 2 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^{6}\ \text{ns} = 2\ \text{ns}.$$

questions.enonce_markdown:
In the design of a system, a simple model of the system is design and used to test the Functionality of the new system before creating it.

(a) What is the term given to the simple design model? (1 mark)

(b) State two advantages of designing the simple model before going for the real system. (2 marks)

(c) Give a limitation of this technique. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Term (1 mark).** A **prototype** (the technique is called prototyping).

**(b) Two advantages (2 marks).**

- The users can see and try the working model early and give their opinion, so mistakes and misunderstood requirements are found and corrected **before** the real system is built, which saves time and money.
- It reduces the risk of failure and increases user satisfaction, because the final system is closer to what the users really need; it also allows the developers to check that the system is feasible.

**(c) One limitation (1 mark).** Building the prototype takes extra time and cost, and the users may think that the prototype is the finished system and expect the final product at once (it may also not show how the real system will perform with many users or large amounts of data).
